question: The machine will not move / won't drive

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Hi, this is Jason with Etnyre Customer Support. I have your Chip Spreader Variable Hopper pulled up here. What can I help you with today?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: The machine will not move / won't drive

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Sorry to hear that. Before we start pulling things apart, let's rule out the simple causes. Is the display showing any alarm at the moment?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Yes, that is correct. No alarms showing. What does the manual say I should check?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Alright. Here's the first step. The computer has a start-latch safety that stops the machine moving after the computer starts up. Put the Park Drive switch into park, then put the joystick in neutral. Now move the Park Drive switch across to drive, and try the joystick again. Let me know when you've done that and I'll walk you through the next step.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Done. What is the next step?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Second thing to check is the speed setpoint - it may simply be set too low. Push the speed toggle switch up, or press one of the memory buttons. The display will show you the new setpoint while it's changing. Tell me what it reads.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Done. What is the next step?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Next is the brake pressure switch, and I need to give you a safety warning before you do this one. Shut the machine off. Unplug the electrical connector on the brake pressure switch - it's on the hose coming off the foot pedal. Now, with that connector unplugged, the service brake on its own will not stop the machine, so make sure you have clear ground around you before you start it again. Start it up and try to move. If it moves now, that switch has failed and needs replacing.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Done. What is the next step?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: The last thing on my list is the charge pressure. You'll want to install a one thousand PSI gauge in port G on the drive pump. With the engine at low idle, that should read approximately four hundred PSI. If it's sitting near zero, the charge pump has failed and that's not a roadside repair - give Etnyre service a call on eight eight eight, five eight six, one eight nine nine and they'll sort you out.
